question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of an organic compound was subjected to estimation of nitrogen by Dumas method in which volume of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> evolved (at STP) was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>22</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math>. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is - [nearest integer] (Given: Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>28</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, Molar volume of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>STP</mi><mo>:</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math>)

solution.text:
Volume of N2 gas is equal to 22.4 ml at STP
Mole of N2 gas = 22.422400=11000
Weight of N2 gas =11000X 28

% of N in organic compound =281000X 1000.2=14%

Hence, The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is 14%
